text:
Philip Broberg scored in St. Louis's comeback from 4-1 down at New Jersey on Thursday, one of two quick goals that tied it 4-4 (Mike Fink, The Hockey News), before the Blues lost in overtime. Nights like that have become normal. He has ten points in his last ten games, he's playing 24 and a half minutes a night and topped 28 in each of his last two, and our breakout flag is on: he's on the ice for 52% of the Blues' power-play chances, up from 28% last season.

The skating is elite; his top speed ranks at the very top of the league. The question is how much of the points pace is real. The Blues have scored about seven more goals than their chances deserved with him on the ice, and at five on five they're almost six points worse in expected-goal share with him out there than without. So the role is real and growing, and the points are running ahead of it. Our projection's middle case is 11 more goals, after six all of last season.
headline: The role is real; the points are running ahead
